prerequisites: Competencies from basic modules in Computer Science are recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Students can explain and apply the most important AI methods and their practical application.
Students can create knowledge-based inference systems in predicate logic (Prolog).
Students can use knowledge representation forms.
Students can present problem-solving, search, and planning algorithms.
Students can provide an overview of common estimation methods, such as Bayes, Dempster/Shafer, Fuzzy Inference.
Students can apply methods of knowledge acquisition from the field of machine learning and knowledge engineering.
Students can gain insight into non-classical logics.
Students are able to apply scientific working methods in independently identifying, formulating, and solving problems.
Students are able to speak freely about scientific content, both in front of an audience and in a discussion.

syllabus_topics: Programming in Prolog / Predicate Logic / Constraints
Practice of knowledge-based systems / Agent systems

assessment_methods.method: Oral presentation of solution for at least two exercise assignments

assessment_rules: To acquire credit points, students must achieve at least 50 percent of the points from the weekly exercise assignments and present the solution of at least two exercise assignments orally. The examination is either an oral exam (individual) or a written exam. Grading is on a scale of 0 to 15 points according to the examination regulations for the M.Sc. Computer Science degree program.
bibliography: W.F. Clocksin, C.S. Mellish: Programming in Prolog, Springer, 2003.
S. Russell, P. Norvig. Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach. Prentice Hall, 2002.
